steps.title: Bronze: land as-is
steps.caption: Bronze: records from all three sources land unchanged, bad ones included, plus load metadata.
steps.body: Change events from the orders database, the clickstream and a partner's daily CSV file are **appended unchanged** to bronze tables, together with ingestion metadata (source, load time, batch ID). Today that is 1,000 order records, **12 duplicates and 3 malformed records included**: bronze fixes nothing and throws nothing away, so it is the complete, replayable history of what the sources sent.

steps.title: Silver: clean and conform
steps.caption: Silver: a job reads new rows, drops 12 duplicates and conforms codes; 3 go to quarantine, 985 pass.
steps.body: A silver job reads **only the new bronze records**, parses and types the fields, removes the 12 duplicates by order ID, converts country names to ISO codes and amounts to one currency, and joins customer data. The 3 malformed records move to a **quarantine table** with the reason, so silver holds **985 validated records** (1,000 − 12 − 3): the trusted, record-level view that many uses share.

steps.title: Gold: shape for use
steps.caption: Gold: silver is aggregated and modelled into business tables, one for each audience.
steps.body: A gold job aggregates and models silver into **business-level tables** for each audience: daily revenue by region for the BI dashboard, a customer features table for the ML model and a product summary (from the clickstream) for the data API. Gold tables are named in business terms, optimised for reading and governed per audience.

steps.title: Fix and replay
steps.caption: A currency bug is fixed and replayed from bronze; lineage shows which tables and consumers it hit.
steps.body: A bug is found in the currency conversion. The silver job is fixed and **replayed from bronze**, which still holds every raw record. **Lineage** shows that only the orders path is affected (two gold tables, the dashboard and the model), and the table format's **time travel** lets the team compare the old and new versions. Day to day, every hop processes only new data, by streaming or incremental merges.
